name: Borehole
author: E. T. Carter
description: A geological borehole seen straight down from above, plunging to a true-black focal point, off-centre by default and movable. Fine sedimentary bands of faintly glowing rock are sliced from log-radius, scuffed by angular drill-grain, and tinted through the palette by depth; an exponential fog drowns the deep walls in black. The whole stack of strata sinks steadily down the scale axis toward a center it never reaches; the pointer parallax-shifts the near walls for a look-around into the bore.

params.label: Descent speed
params.effect: Scale-octaves per second the strata sink toward the dark center of the bore.

params.label: Band density
params.effect: Sediment bands per scale octave — higher packs finer, more numerous rings down the wall.

params.label: Fog depth
params.effect: How far down the bore light reaches before black swallows the walls; low values shrink the lit annulus toward the rim.

params.label: Grain
params.effect: Amount of angular drill-grain scuffing the bands — 0 leaves clean concentric rings.

params.label: Focal X
params.effect: Horizontal offset of the bore's dark focal point — off-centre by default for an asymmetric, off-axis plunge.

params.label: Focal Y
params.effect: Vertical offset of the bore's focal point out of dead-centre.

params.label: Mouse parallax
params.effect: How far the near walls slide toward the pointer for a depth look-around (the deep core holds; no effect on the static poster).
